messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: KV cache memory growth alert on cluster tp-shard-pool-4. Sustained >80% for 5m, 4/8 GPUs reporting OOMs, NCCL timeouts observed. Creating incident thread.
Alex: i'm on it, grabbing logs and metrics now.
Morgan: seeing a big spike that lines up with the continuous-batching rollout ~08:12 UTC on prod. might be related.
Samir: if batching params changed we could be packing too much into KV cache -> blowup. can you confirm what changed?
Lee: rollout diff shows batcher.max_batch_size 256 -> 1024 and continuous_batching.enabled=true. that looks risky.
Tia: quick triage Q — are customers seeing errors or is this internal only? need to know comms.
Alex: telemetry shows p50/p95 latency up, error rate +3.2% in us-west-2. one customer reported degraded throughput via support. no total outage.
Morgan: dmesg/NCCL logs show "NCCL WARN Allgather timeout" and repeated call failures. pattern looks like uneven shard load on tp shards.
Samir: thought: allocator may have produced an uneven partition during the last rollout. hotspot -> GPU OOM -> NCCL stalls. we should revert batching and rebalance shards.
Lee: mitigation plan (short):
- Abort continuous batching (flip feature flag) immediate
- Revert max_batch_size to conservative value
- Trigger shard rebalancer (staged)
- If NCCL still fails, fall back affected model routes to single-gpu path
Alex: executing step 1 now.
incident-bot: Deploy action started by Alex:
```
/deploy toggle continuous_batching=false --env prod --pool tp-shard-pool-4
```
Alex: toggle applied. observability: queue length dropping on most nodes, mem usage leveling on 3/4 GPUs, one host still climbing.
Morgan: running rebalancer probe. mapping shows shard id 7 duplicated across GPU0 and GPU1 due to race during prior rollout — hotspot confirmed.
Samir: preparing small allocator patch to enforce stable-hash mapping and strict single-owner invariant. i'll canary on 2 nodes before wider roll.
Tia: opened ticket INC-5543 for the customer report and notified CS.
Lee: canary live on 2 nodes. monitoring NCCL output.
Alex: post-toggle metrics: p95 latency trending down, error rate returning toward baseline in us-west-2. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: NCCL timeouts still present on host i-0a12cd3f; suggests daemon stuck or local GPU driver issue.
Samir: sshing to i-0a12cd3f and restarting nccl-daemon + inference-worker.
Samir: command run:
```
ssh ubuntu@i-0a12cd3f 'sudo systemctl restart nccl-daemon && sudo systemctl restart inference-worker'
```
Samir: restart completed, worker rejoined cluster. NCCL timeouts cleared on that host.
Morgan: rebalancer sweep completed across pool, shard distribution now even. memory pressure normalized across nodes.
Tia: customer update sent by support: "throughput improving, thank you" — CS will follow up.
Lee: post-incident action items so far:
- root cause: continuous-batching rollout + allocator race -> uneven shard mapping -> GPU hotspot -> NCCL stalls
- short-term mitigations: revert batching, rebalancer, targeted restarts
- long-term fixes: allocator invariant patch, stricter canary gating for batching changes, automated shard health checks, extra telemetry around per-shard memory
- impact estimate: ~12h engineering time, 1 customer SLO blip, sev2 classification
Alex: oncall handoff in 40m to Morgan. compiling notes and run commands.
Morgan: taking handoff. will run extended compaction / stress for a few hours and validate the allocator hotfix rollout tomorrow 02:00 UTC.
incident-bot: Handoff recorded: Alex -> Morgan at 20:00 UTC. refer to incident runbook step 4 for follow up tasks.
Lee: pushed patch link: https://git.redwood/infra/allocator/commit/abc123 (hotfix enforces stable-hash + single-owner).
Samir: hotfix tag v2.1.4-hotfix created and canaryed. scheduling full rollout at 02:00 UTC tomorrow.
Tia: flagging accounts team to notify customers in impacted region during maintenance window.
Alex: will file postmortem with timeline, attach logs and commands.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated. severity: Sev2. incident-id: INC-2026-042. Closing this channel after postmortem is filed. :lock_with_key:
